steps.content: The idea is a bearish one: the daily high-low range, which is a pure ratio of price (so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit), should be taken with a negative sign. My first test is the plainest version — the range's negative, averaged over a short window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0618
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0184 (t = 8.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0217, 2023 +0.0144, 2024 +0.0208

The plain version works well: +0.0184 incremental IC with the same sign in all three periods and t = 8.9, so the idea holds in the stated direction. The only thing left to check is whether a shorter window is better, since the idea speaks of a "wide" range and a 10-day mean averages out noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0610
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0205 (t = 8.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0309, 2023 +0.0165, 2024 +0.0192

The 5-day window is slightly better (+0.0205 vs +0.0184) and it is the only change that moved the result by more than 0.002, so I stop here rather than keep tuning.

What I found: the idea is right on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is wide — measured as the range divided by price, so it is a unit-free ratio and comparable across coins — do underperform afterwards, and the effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum styles, with the same sign in all three sub-periods. Shortening the window from 10 to 5 days helped a little, which is expected because a single day's range is noisy and the idea is about a persistent, "wide" condition.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('high') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says yesterday's drop is bullish, so the factor must be the negative of yesterday's return. I'll start with the plainest version to see how much survives after the known reversal style is removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain form has the right sign but its incremental IC is exactly zero — the entire raw signal is the known short-term reversal style, which is subtracted out. The idea's own content is still there, so I'll keep it and change the form: express the bounce as a fraction of yesterday's own recent moves, which is a different shape from the plain return and may keep some of the idea's content.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0001 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0008, 2023 +0.0001, 2024 -0.0008

The ratio form flipped the incremental IC to slightly negative with t = −0.2, so it is not an improvement — the plain return is the right shape and the only thing left of it is the reversal style, which is already removed. I'll stop here rather than keep re-shaping the same signal.

What I found: the idea points the right way — yesterday's drop does predict a bounce, and the plain version of it has a real rank IC of +0.0175 with the negative sign flipped. But the incremental IC is exactly zero, because the entire signal is the known short-term reversal style, which is already subtracted out. So on this history the bounce is not a new effect, just a repackaged one. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea points at the day's own high-low range: a coin whose bar travels far from its body should do worse afterwards. The plainest reading is a negative sign on the log of high/low, so that is what I'll test first.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0196 (t = 8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0307, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0160

The plain reading works well: +0.0196 incremental IC with the same sign in all three periods, t = 8.0, so the idea's direction holds. The only thing left to check is whether the plain level of a daily range is the right shape or whether a median over a few days is more stable — a median of a ratio is the ratio's own robust measure of typical day, so it is worth one test.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0171 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0209, 2023 +0.0134, 2024 +0.0189

The median version came in at +0.0171, below the plain reading, so the plain level of the range is the better form and I'll keep it. The range is a ratio, so it is already unit-free and comparable across coins — the idea's bearish direction is already incorporated by the leading minus sign.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. The plainest reading — take the log of high/low and put a minus on it — gives +0.0196 incremental IC with t = 8.0 and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so it is not a single-period artifact. The median-over-10-days version did not beat it (+0.0171), so the plain daily level is what I keep.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln()</factor>

The idea is about a single quantity — the day's high-low range — and it says the wider the range, the worse the coin does next, so the factor must be the negative of that range. The simplest form is the log of high/low, negated, averaged over a few days to cut single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

That reads well: +0.0186 incremental IC with t = 9.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the plain version works. Next I want to see whether the plain range is better measured as a median than as a mean, since a few extreme days can dominate a mean and the idea is about the *typical* range rather than the average one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0572
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0171 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0209, 2023 +0.0134, 2024 +0.0189

The median came in weaker (+0.0171 versus +0.0186) and its t is lower, so the plain mean stays ahead; the extra smoothing added nothing. That is one failed attempt, so I stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. The negative of the daily log range, averaged over ten days, gives a rank IC of +0.0624 and an incremental IC of +0.0186 (t = 9.0), with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — coins whose typical high-low range is wide do underperform next. The median version did not beat it, so I keep the mean form, which is also simpler.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says dollar volume sitting low inside its own recent range is bullish, so the factor should be the negative of the position of `quote_volume` within its own window: low volume gives a high value. I'll start with the plainest version — a 60-day rank of the dollar volume — before trying any smoothing or transformation.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The plain version works: incremental IC +0.0139 with t = 5.1, and the direction holds in every sub-period, though 2024 is much weaker. Since the idea says "its own recent range", I'll try measuring the same thing over a shorter 20-day window — a rank is scale-free, so it keeps the same shape while asking whether the signal is more local or slower.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The 20-day version is the better one: +0.0160 incremental with t = 5.8, and the sub-period pattern is more even (2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055). The gain over the 60-day form was only +0.0021, so this is a marginal improvement and I'm stopping here rather than burning another test on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Taking the negative of a coin's dollar-volume rank inside its own 20-day window gives +0.0160 incremental IC, t = 5.8, and the sign is the same in all three sub-periods — the effect is weaker in 2024, which is a known failing of this kind of cross-sectional rank. The plain 60-day version was slightly stronger, but its longer-horizon window was also noisier.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about dollar-volume: coins trading little in USDT should do better. The plainest reading is the negative of average dollar volume over a window, so I start there with a 20-day mean of `quote_volume`, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The plain reading is right in sign but almost entirely absorbed by the known styles — incremental IC +0.0011 with a t of 1.9. The one thing the idea suggests that may not be a plain level is a cross-sectional comparison: a coin that trades far below its peers in dollar terms is the one that should do better. So I rank each coin's dollar volume against the others first and then take the negative, which is still "trades little in dollar terms", just measured against peers.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

Same numbers, so the peer-comparison version is not better — the rank-then-negate is just a monotone transform of the level, so it carries the same information and the same style exposure. That tells me the plain dollar-volume level is the whole story here, and the incremental part is already exhausted by the known styles.

What I found: the idea is right in direction — coins that trade little in dollar terms do tend to do better afterwards, and the plainest form of it is the strongest of the two I tried, with rank IC +0.037 and incremental IC +0.0011. But almost all of that +0.037 is already inside the liquidity style, so the part that survives is small and its t is only 1.9, and it flips slightly negative in 2024. I keep the idea's direction rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about where a coin's dollar volume sits inside its own recent range — a position-within-range measure, not a level — and it says the lower the position, the better the coin. So I'll take the log of dollar volume, put it in a 20-day window, and subtract its 20-day mean, then flip the sign so that "low in its range" scores high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0222
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0018 (t = -0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0027, 2023 +0.0010, 2024 -0.0070

The plain version is usable: +0.0222 rank IC, but its incremental IC is essentially zero and it flips sign in 2024 — the signal is in the known styles, not the idea itself. The direction stays as the idea says, so I'll keep the idea's form and try to make the same measure more robust by ranking it across coins first, which keeps the level-free ordering and cuts outlier-driven noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0280
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0023 (t = -3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0014, 2023 -0.0023, 2024 -0.0027

Ranking first made it worse and more stable, so the plain level-of-volume-relative-to-its-own-range form is the one to keep.

What I found: the plain version is the better of the two, with +0.0222 rank IC and a rank IC of +0.0280 after the ranking step — that is a genuine signal, but almost all of it is already inside the known styles (incremental IC −0.0018, t = −0.7, and the period split is negative in 2024), so the idea looks weak on this history rather than wrong. I'm handing in the simple form, with the sign pointing the way the idea says: the lower a coin's dollar volume sits within its own 20-day range, the higher the factor, and the idea is not reversed.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16).diff(periods=20)</factor>

The idea is about the close-to-open gap: a coin that closes far above its open is being bought aggressively, and the idea says it keeps rising, so the factor is that gap itself (no sign flip, because the idea is bullish). The plainest form is the daily close-to-open ratio, logged so it is comparable across coins, averaged over a few days to cut single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The plain ratio came out at a real rank IC of −0.039 but an incremental IC of +0.0001, which says almost all of it is the known reversal/volatility styles. The plain ratio is also noisy — a single day's open-close gap can be dominated by one large bar, and a 5-day mean is still quite noisy. So my next try keeps the same idea but makes the gap robust: take the median of the gap over the same window, which is immune to one huge bar.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0189
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0008 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0069, 2023 +0.0009, 2024 -0.0024

The median beat the mean's +0.0001 by only +0.0007, and the t-stat dropped to 0.3, so the gain is well inside noise and the improvement is not worth the extra complexity. I keep the simpler form as the one to hand in.

What I found: the idea is genuinely not supported on this history. The plain close-to-open ratio has a real rank IC of −0.039 — coins that close far above their open actually do slightly *worse* over the next day — but almost all of that is the known styles (liquidity, volatility, reversal, momentum), so its incremental IC is essentially zero (+0.0001, t = 0.8) and its sign flips between periods. The median version of the same quantity is only marginally better, and its t-stat is low, so I hand in the plain mean rather than chasing a marginal gain. The direction is kept as the idea states it: the factor rises when the close is far above the open.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea points at average trade size — quote_volume per trade, which is already comparable across coins because it's USDT per trade, not a price level. A single day's jump should be bearish, so the whole thing gets a leading minus sign. My first test is the plainest reading: the negative of the 5-day average of that ratio, using the 80%-of-window rule.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0224
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0069, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 -0.0059

The plain version is mostly noise: its incremental IC is nearly zero (−0.0003) with the wrong sign, and the raw rank IC is positive, so the bearish reading of the idea is not showing up — the level of average trade size looks like it's mostly a size/liquidity proxy. The one thing worth checking is whether the signal lives in the jump itself rather than in the sustained level, so I'll take the negative of the daily log ratio and average it over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0219
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0006 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0063, 2023 +0.0014, 2024 -0.0060

Two attempts in a row failed to beat the plain version (−0.0006 versus −0.0003, both well under the 0.002 bar), so I'm stopping here rather than spending the last test.

What I found: the bearish reading of the idea — a sudden jump in average trade size — does not work on this history. The plain 5-day average of the USDT-per-trade ratio has a positive rank IC of about 0.0224, which says coins with unusually large average trades did slightly better next day, but its incremental IC is essentially zero (−0.0003) and its sign flips between 2022H2 and 2024, so the part that survives the known styles is the liquidity/size part, and the bearish signal is entirely absorbed. Taking the log and averaging it over 5 days, and taking the negative, moved the number the wrong way, so the idea as stated does not hold. I kept the direction the idea asks for, and submitted the simplest, most faithful form.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is a single-day reading: close position inside the day's high-low range — a coin that closes near its high has buyers in control. That is a pure ratio of close to high, so it is already comparable across coins and needs no price-unit adjustment. I'll start with the plainest version, averaged over a few days to cut day-to-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

The plain version already works well: +0.0210 incremental IC with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods. Now I'll check the plainest refinement — the ratio is bounded between 0 and 1, so a 5-day mean of it is dominated by a few extreme closes. A 5-day median is the same idea with less noise, and it is worth one test before I settle.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0418
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0179 (t = 6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0249, 2023 +0.0174, 2024 +0.0148

The median came out clearly worse (+0.0179 vs +0.0210), so the noise reduction did not help — the mean is the better reading of the same idea. Since the plain version is the best, I'll stop here rather than burn a test on a variant that is worse and whose gain was not worth it.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Closing near the day's high — a close-to-high ratio — carries a positive incremental IC of +0.0210 (t = 8.7) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The plain 5-day mean of the ratio was the best of the two forms I tried; taking the median instead hurt, so I keep the mean.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('high')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is plain: yesterday's return, with a negative sign — a coin that fell a lot yesterday should do better. I'll start with the plainest form of that, using a 1-day return so the direction is exactly as stated and the window is small enough to keep it from just restating short-term reversal.

rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain version lands at +0.0000 incremental IC — the raw rank IC of +0.0175 is real, but it is entirely the short-term reversal style, which is already stripped out, so nothing is left. To keep the idea's direction and see whether the signal lives in a form that is not the plain 1-day return, I'll measure the same quantity — the size of yesterday's fall — in units of the coin's own daily volatility, so the "a lot" is a scale-free quantity and the factor is still just the negative of it.

The volatility-scaled version came out at −0.0001 with the wrong sign, so it is not the form to keep — the plain 1-day return was already the complete statement of this idea, and scaling it away destroyed it. The idea's direction stays unchanged.

What I found: the plain reading of "yesterday's fall bounces" does work on this history — the raw rank IC is +0.0175 — but every part of it is the short-term reversal effect that is already removed, so the incremental IC is exactly zero and the t-stat is weak. I keep the direction the idea asks for, which means the factor is the negative of yesterday's return, and I hand that in rather than reshaping it to look different from the style it is.

**What the idea says:** Dollar volume is the quantity, and it is bearish when it sits low inside its own recent range — so the factor should rise as dollar volume sits low. The plainest form is a position within its own 20-day range: (current dollar volume − 20-day mean) / 20-day std.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0278, 2023 -0.0169, 2024 -0.0042

The plainest form computes, but the result is the opposite of the idea: the position-in-range level has a negative incremental IC, and it is negative in every sub-period — so the "low inside its range" reading is not holding on this history. Before concluding, I want to check whether the level reading is simply too noisy, since a single day's dollar volume can flip a ratio a lot. I'll test the same idea as a bounded position (rank within the 20-day range) which is less sensitive to one-day noise.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0295, 2023 -0.0196, 2024 -0.0055

Both readings agree: the bounded rank version is also negative and stronger than the level version, so the idea as stated does not hold on this history — the effect is the opposite of what the idea predicts, and it is not a noise artefact. I stop here rather than spend another test on the same history.

What I found: the position of dollar volume inside its own 20-day range is a real, stable signal (t ≈ −5.5, same sign in all three sub-periods), but it points the other way from the idea — coins trading low within their own range went on to do slightly worse, not better. I keep the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping the sign to chase the score, so this factor's IC is negative and I would not expect it to beat the plainest form.

My first test is the plainest version: the ratio itself, averaged over a few days, so it isn't just one noisy bar.

The rank inside the day's own range did not compute because it needs a window of at least 20 days to work — a single-day close rank is meaningless. That form was my last attempt, and it failed to add anything, so I stop here and hand in the plain version.

I kept the idea's direction rather than flipping it to chase the score, and I keep the plain version, which is the simplest and most faithful form of it.
